Source format: Board meeting minutes

- **Action 2025-02-01 (Mr. Osei):** Draft revised treasury management policy – completed, circulated 20 February.
- **Action 2025-02-03 (Ms. Hartley):** Report on unplanned outages at Westlea pumping station – completed, presented at this meeting under item 7.
- **Action 2025-02-05 (Mr. Ashworth):** Update on insurance renewal discussions – completed; summary provided in risk register update (item 6).

No further matters arising were raised.

## 4. Financial Reports

Mr. Osei presented the management accounts for the period ending 28 February 2025.

### 4.1 Income and Expenditure Summary
The operating result for the eleven months to 28 February 2025 showed a surplus of £612,000, which was £84,000 favourable to the budget. The favourable variance was attributed mainly to lower-than-expected energy costs and reduced contractor spend on reactive maintenance.

### 4.2 Capital Expenditure
Year-to-date capital expenditure stood at £3.4 million against a full-year budget of £5.8 million. Mr. Osei noted that the pace of spend was expected to accelerate in March as several projects reached completion milestones.

### 4.3 Cash Position
Cash balances as at 28 February stood at £2.1 million. This was within the target range set by the treasury management policy. Mr. Osei drew the Board's attention to the forthcoming payment schedule for the Wroughton main replacement, with a milestone payment of £480,000 due in mid-April.

### 4.4 Debtors and Creditors
Trade debtors aged over 90 days remained low at £38,000. Mr. Osei confirmed that the largest overdue balance, relating to a commercial customer in the Old Town area, had been reduced to £12,000 following a payment arrangement.

## 5. Risk Register Update

Mr. Ashworth presented the quarterly review of the corporate risk register.

### 5.1 Key Changes Since Last Review

- **Risk R-14 (Aging infrastructure – trunk mains):** Likelihood increased from Possible (3) to Likely (4) following the two unplanned bursts in February. Residual risk score increased from 12 to 16, above the Board's agreed tolerance of 15. A mitigation action to accelerate the condition assessment of the affected section has been added.
- **Risk R-07 (Key person dependency – control room):** Likelihood reduced from Likely (4) to Possible (3) following the successful completion of the controller training programme in February. Residual risk score reduced from 12 to 9.
- **Risk R-21 (Supply chain – chlorine shortage):** No change to scoring, but the mitigating action to maintain a six-week buffer stock has been verified as operating correctly.

### 5.2 New Risk
Mr. Ashworth reported a new risk, R-27, relating to the potential impact of proposed changes to the Water Industry National Environment Programme on future capital requirements. The initial risk score was assessed as 8 (Likelihood 2, Impact 4). A full assessment will be presented at the April meeting.

### 5.3 Risk Appetite Confirmation
The Chair noted that the residual risk scores for all risks remained within the Board's stated risk appetite, with the exception of R-14, which was now above tolerance. Mr. Ashworth confirmed that a mitigation plan would be presented at the April meeting.

## 6. Capital Budget Approval – Reservoir Upgrade

Ms. Hartley introduced the item, noting that the reservoir upgrade project had been in development since late 2024. The project scope included:

- Refurbishment of the 12 megalitre concrete reservoir serving the northern zone
- Replacement of the inlet and outlet valve chambers
- Installation of a new telemetry system for remote level monitoring
- Re-lining of the internal surfaces to prevent further water quality degradation

Ms. Hartley reported that the current asset had experienced repeated water quality exceedances in 2024, with three instances of elevated turbidity recorded between June and September. The interim mitigation measures, including increased flushing and additional sampling, had been effective but were not sustainable in the long term.
### 7.3 Water Quality and Customer Committee

Ms. Hartley reported that the Water Quality and Customer Committee had met on 18 March 2025. The Committee had reviewed the customer complaint statistics for the period January to February 2025. A total of 214 complaints had been received, compared with 186 in the corresponding period in 2024. The increase was primarily attributable to billing enquiries following the implementation of the new billing system in November 2024. The Committee noted that the number of complaints relating to water quality had remained stable, at 23 in the two-month period.

The Committee had also reviewed the results of the quarterly customer satisfaction survey. The overall satisfaction score was eighty-one percent, a slight decrease from the eighty-four percent recorded in the previous quarter. The Committee noted that the decrease was within the normal range of variation and did not indicate a systemic issue.

## 8. Organisational Update

Ms. Hartley provided the Board with an update on the organisational structure of the Company. She confirmed that the current reporting lines remained unchanged and that the structure continued to operate effectively. In particular, she noted that the operational teams continued to report to the Operations Manager, and that the Operations Manager reports directly to the Board of Directors, a line of accountability that has been in place since the Company's establishment and remains current. Ms. Hartley confirmed that no changes to the structure were proposed during the current financial year.

Ms. Hartley also reported that the recruitment process for two new engineering technician posts had been completed. The posts had been advertised in February 2025 and a total of 34 applications had been received. Following shortlisting and interviews, offers had been made to two candidates, both of whom had accepted. The successful candidates were expected to commence employment on 28 April 2025 and 12 May 2025 respectively.

In response to a question from Mr. Fletcher regarding succession planning, Ms. Hartley confirmed that a succession plan for key management roles had been developed and would be presented to the Board at the April meeting. The plan covered the roles of Operations Manager, Finance Manager, and Customer Services Manager.

## 9. Operational Performance Report

Ms. Hartley presented the operational performance report for the period January to February 2025.

### 9.1 Water Quality

Ms. Hartley reported that water quality compliance for the period was ninety-nine point nine percent, in line with the Company's target of one hundred percent and the regulatory minimum of ninety-nine point nine five percent. A total of 4,872 samples had been taken during the period, of which 4,867 had met the required standards.

The five non-compliant samples were as follows:

- Two samples taken from a customer tap in the Old Town area in January, which exceeded the iron standard of two hundred micrograms per litre. The cause was identified as sediment disturbance following a mains repair on Queens Drive. Follow-up samples taken after flushing were compliant.
- One sample taken from a service reservoir in the eastern zone in February, which exceeded the turbidity standard of four nephelometric turbidity units. The cause was identified as an algal bloom in the reservoir. The reservoir was taken out of service, cleaned, and returned to service on 24 February.
- Two samples taken from a customer tap in the Westlea area in February, which exceeded the manganese standard of fifty micrograms per litre. The cause was identified as a localised issue with the distribution network. Flushing was undertaken and follow-up samples were compliant.

Ms. Hartley confirmed that the Drinking Water Inspectorate had been notified of all five exceedances in accordance with the required timescales. No formal enforcement action had been taken.
Mr. Pemberton reported that the bad debt provision had been increased by £150,000 to £1.2 million, reflecting a small rise in the number of household accounts falling into arrears during the winter period. He noted that the Company's collection rate remained above the industry average.

### 10.4 Financial Risk

The Board noted the key financial risks set out in the risk register, including the potential impact of further interest rate rises on the Company's variable rate borrowing. Mr. Pemberton confirmed that the Company's hedging arrangements covered approximately seventy percent of its debt portfolio until March 2026.

The Board approved the finance report.

**Motion:** That the finance report for the period ending 28 February 2025 be received and noted.  
**Proposed by:** Mr. Pemberton  
**Seconded by:** Ms. Hartley  
**Vote:** All in favour.  
**Action 10.1:** Mr. Pemberton to circulate the revised capital programme forecast to the Board by 21 March 2025.

## 11. Project Updates

### 11.1 Queens Drive Mains Replacement

Mr. Chen, Lead Engineer, provided an update on the Queens Drive mains replacement project. The project was progressing to schedule, with approximately sixty percent of the new main laid. Mr. Chen reported that the project remained within budget and that disruption to local residents had been minimised through the use of temporary traffic management.

The Board noted that the project was expected to be completed by the end of June 2025, subject to favourable weather conditions.

### 11.2 Service Reservoir Cleaning Programme

Mr. Chen reported that the annual service reservoir cleaning programme had commenced in February. Three of the Company's twelve service reservoirs had been cleaned to date. The programme was on track to be completed by September 2025.

### 11.3 Leakage Reduction Initiative

Mr. Chen updated the Board on the leakage reduction initiative. The Company was currently achieving a leakage level of 18.5 percent of distribution input, against a regulatory target of 17.5 percent. A trial of acoustic loggers in the Old Town area had identified a number of previously undetected leaks, which were being repaired.

Mr. Fletcher asked whether the trial would be extended to other areas. Mr. Chen confirmed that an assessment of the trial's cost effectiveness would be presented to the Board at the April meeting.

## 12. Personnel Matters

### 12.1 Appointment of Customer Services Manager

The Board considered the appointment of Mrs. Susan Whitfield to the post of Customer Services Manager. Mrs. Whitfield had been acting in the role since January 2025 and had performed well during that period.

**Motion:** That Mrs. Susan Whitfield be appointed to the post of Customer Services Manager, with effect from 1 April 2025, on the terms and conditions set out in the personnel committee report.  
**Proposed by:** Ms. Hartley  
**Seconded by:** Mr. Fletcher  
**Vote:** All in favour.  
**Action 12.1:** The Company Secretary to issue the contract of employment to Mrs. Whitfield.

### 12.2 Professional Qualifications of Staff

Ms. Hartley reported that the Company continued to place a high priority on the professional development of its staff. She noted that the Company employed a number of staff holding recognised professional qualifications, including engineers, accountants, and environmental scientists.

In response to a question from Mr. Fletcher, Ms. Hartley confirmed that the Company's records showed that Mr. David Chen, Lead Engineer, holds the professional license of Chartered Engineer (CEng). Ms. Hartley noted that this qualification was a current and valid requirement for the role and that the Company's HR records were kept up to date in this regard.

### 12.3 Staff Training

Ms. Hartley reported that the Company had spent £18,000 on staff training during the first two months of the year, covering areas such as water quality sampling, health and safety, and customer service. A further £45,000 was budgeted for the remainder of the year.
Ms. Hartley reported that the Board currently comprised seven members, including the Chair. She noted that, following the retirement of Mr. Alan Pemberton in December 2024, the Board had operated with one vacancy. The appointments committee had been considering suitable candidates and expected to bring a recommendation to the Board before the summer recess.

Mr. Fletcher observed that the Board had not yet considered whether the size of the Board remained appropriate. Ms. Hartley confirmed that the matter could be included in the agenda for the June meeting, should members wish. No motion was tabled.

### 13.4 Declaration of Interest – Contract for Metering Works

Mr. Chen declared a personal interest in the contract for metering works at the Queens Drive depot, insofar as his brother-in-law was employed by the successful contractor, Thames Valley Metering Ltd. Mr. Chen confirmed that he would take no part in any discussion or decision relating to that contract. The declaration was noted.

## 14. Committee Reports

### 14.1 Audit Committee

Mr. Fletcher, as Chair of the Audit Committee, reported that the committee had met on 28 May 2025. The committee had reviewed the draft annual accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 and had received the external auditors' management letter. The auditors had raised no material matters, although they had recommended that the Company review its procedures for the authorisation of overtime. The committee had accepted this recommendation and had asked the Finance Manager to prepare a revised procedure for approval at the next committee meeting.

### 14.2 Personnel Committee

Ms. Hartley reported that the Personnel Committee had met on 2 June 2025. The committee had considered the outcome of the staff appraisal cycle and had noted that ninety-two percent of appraisals had been completed by the end of May. The committee had also reviewed the sickness absence statistics for the first five months of the year, which showed an average of three point four days per employee. This was slightly higher than the same period in the previous year, and the committee had asked the HR Officer to investigate the reasons.

### 14.3 Remuneration Committee

Mrs. Whitmore reported, in her capacity as a member of the Remuneration Committee, that the committee had met on 27 May 2025. The committee had reviewed the salaries of senior managers in accordance with the Company's pay policy. No changes were proposed for the current financial year, other than those already provided for in the annual budget.

## 15. Risk Register Update

Mr. Chen presented an update to the Board's risk register. He noted that the risk relating to the failure of the bulk supply from Thames Water remained at its existing rating, with mitigating actions ongoing. The risk relating to the condition of the Victoria Road pumping station had been reduced from high to medium, following the completion of the refurbishment of the standby generator.

Mr. Chen also reported that a new risk had been added to the register, relating to the potential impact of a prolonged heatwave on water demand and the availability of supply. This risk had been assessed as having a low likelihood but a high impact, and a number of mitigating actions had been identified, including the preparation of a communications plan for customers.

Mr. Fletcher asked whether the risk register would be reviewed at the next meeting. Mr. Chen confirmed that a full review was scheduled for the July meeting, and that any changes to risk ratings would be reported to the Board at that time.

## 16. Any Other Business

### 16.1 Community Engagement Event

Mrs. Whitmore reported that the Company had been invited to take part in a community engagement event at the Old Town Hall on Saturday 21 June 2025. The event was being organised by the Swindon Civic Society and would provide an opportunity for residents to learn more about the Company's operations. Mrs. Whitmore suggested that the Company should have a stall at the event, staffed by members of the customer services team, and that information about the Company's water efficiency scheme should be made available.

documents.title: Swindon Water Services Board Meeting Minutes – 2025-03-05
documents.content:
- **Action 2025-02-01 (Mr. Osei):** Draft revised treasury management policy – completed, circulated 20 February.
- **Action 2025-02-03 (Ms. Hartley):** Report on unplanned outages at Westlea pumping station – completed, presented at this meeting under item 7.
- **Action 2025-02-05 (Mr. Ashworth):** Update on insurance renewal discussions – completed; summary provided in risk register update (item 6).

No further matters arising were raised.

## 4. Financial Reports

Mr. Osei presented the management accounts for the period ending 28 February 2025.

### 4.1 Income and Expenditure Summary
The operating result for the eleven months to 28 February 2025 showed a surplus of £612,000, which was £84,000 favourable to the budget. The favourable variance was attributed mainly to lower-than-expected energy costs and reduced contractor spend on reactive maintenance.

### 4.2 Capital Expenditure
Year-to-date capital expenditure stood at £3.4 million against a full-year budget of £5.8 million. Mr. Osei noted that the pace of spend was expected to accelerate in March as several projects reached completion milestones.

### 4.3 Cash Position
Cash balances as at 28 February stood at £2.1 million. This was within the target range set by the treasury management policy. Mr. Osei drew the Board's attention to the forthcoming payment schedule for the Wroughton main replacement, with a milestone payment of £480,000 due in mid-April.

### 4.4 Debtors and Creditors
Trade debtors aged over 90 days remained low at £38,000. Mr. Osei confirmed that the largest overdue balance, relating to a commercial customer in the Old Town area, had been reduced to £12,000 following a payment arrangement.

## 5. Risk Register Update

Emily Hartley approved_capital_budget 1250000 GBP. Record status: current.

Mr. Ashworth presented the quarterly review of the corporate risk register.

### 5.1 Key Changes Since Last Review

- **Risk R-14 (Aging infrastructure – trunk mains):** Likelihood increased from Possible (3) to Likely (4) following the two unplanned bursts in February. Residual risk score increased from 12 to 16, above the Board's agreed tolerance of 15. A mitigation action to accelerate the condition assessment of the affected section has been added.
- **Risk R-07 (Key person dependency – control room):** Likelihood reduced from Likely (4) to Possible (3) following the successful completion of the controller training programme in February. Residual risk score reduced from 12 to 9.
- **Risk R-21 (Supply chain – chlorine shortage):** No change to scoring, but the mitigating action to maintain a six-week buffer stock has been verified as operating correctly.

### 5.2 New Risk
Mr. Ashworth reported a new risk, R-27, relating to the potential impact of proposed changes to the Water Industry National Environment Programme on future capital requirements. The initial risk score was assessed as 8 (Likelihood 2, Impact 4). A full assessment will be presented at the April meeting.

### 5.3 Risk Appetite Confirmation
The Chair noted that the residual risk scores for all risks remained within the Board's stated risk appetite, with the exception of R-14, which was now above tolerance. Mr. Ashworth confirmed that a mitigation plan would be presented at the April meeting.

## 6. Capital Budget Approval – Reservoir Upgrade

Ms. Hartley introduced the item, noting that the reservoir upgrade project had been in development since late 2024. The project scope included:

- Refurbishment of the 12 megalitre concrete reservoir serving the northern zone
- Replacement of the inlet and outlet valve chambers
- Installation of a new telemetry system for remote level monitoring
- Re-lining of the internal surfaces to prevent further water quality degradation

Ms. Hartley reported that the current asset had experienced repeated water quality exceedances in 2024, with three instances of elevated turbidity recorded between June and September. The interim mitigation measures, including increased flushing and additional sampling, had been effective but were not sustainable in the long term.

### 7.3 Water Quality and Customer Committee

Ms. Hartley reported that the Water Quality and Customer Committee had met on 18 March 2025. The Committee had reviewed the customer complaint statistics for the period January to February 2025. A total of 214 complaints had been received, compared with 186 in the corresponding period in 2024. The increase was primarily attributable to billing enquiries following the implementation of the new billing system in November 2024. The Committee noted that the number of complaints relating to water quality had remained stable, at 23 in the two-month period.

The Committee had also reviewed the results of the quarterly customer satisfaction survey. The overall satisfaction score was eighty-one percent, a slight decrease from the eighty-four percent recorded in the previous quarter. The Committee noted that the decrease was within the normal range of variation and did not indicate a systemic issue.

## 8. Organisational Update

The five non-compliant samples were as follows:

- Two samples taken from a customer tap in the Old Town area in January, which exceeded the iron standard of two hundred micrograms per litre. The cause was identified as sediment disturbance following a mains repair on Queens Drive. Follow-up samples taken after flushing were compliant.
- One sample taken from a service reservoir in the eastern zone in February, which exceeded the turbidity standard of four nephelometric turbidity units. The cause was identified as an algal bloom in the reservoir. The reservoir was taken out of service, cleaned, and returned to service on 24 February.
- Two samples taken from a customer tap in the Westlea area in February, which exceeded the manganese standard of fifty micrograms per litre. The cause was identified as a localised issue with the distribution network. Flushing was undertaken and follow-up samples were compliant.
